format.sheet: 1280x1280 RGBA WebP, 320px cells, right-facing. Physically identical to the base/motion/motion2 banks (4x4 geometry, one global scale, feet on the cell floor) so drawAtlasFrame, tintedSilhouette, the crossfade ghost, the palette remap, the damage compositor and the 3D bank builder all read it unchanged. Only ROW 0 carries art: cells 0-3 are the four walk keys, cells 4-15 are empty and are never addressed.
format.grammar: see MOTION-ATLAS.md 'Walk bank (2.10)'. Four keys of ONE stride, generated in ONE pass: 0 contact-left, 1 passing-left, 2 contact-right, 3 passing-right. The cycle plays 0-1-2-3-0. Keys 0 and 2 carry OPPOSITE lead legs; keys 1 and 3 swing opposite legs. Played as its own self-contained bank, NEVER interleaved with the base walk cells.
format.generator: openai-gpt-image-2 via fal MCP (prompt-only; the tool exposes no image parameter, re-confirmed this wave -- identity is carried by per-fighter character bibles written from the base atlas)
format.processed: blob-clustering slicer (walk30/slice4.py): soft magenta key + despill on tools/build_atlas.py conventions, run-length connected components with union-find, each figure masked by its OWN blob labels (a bbox crop drags in the neighbouring figure's arm on a tight filmstrip), ONE global scale for all four keys from the tallest key, foot bottoms registered to the shared floor row 315, torso centroid registered to the cell centre.
format.scaleNote: One global scale per sheet, taken from the TALLEST key so the passing keys keep their genuine extra body height -- the walk's vertical bob comes from the art, never from a per-cell rescale. The tallest key is normalised to the fighter's measured base walk cell height (deathblow 304px, jez 304px), which is how world size is verified against the base bank.
format.acceptNote: Six of ten fighters ship a walk sheet: deathblow and jez from the 2.10 pilot, and post, cyraxx, ali and benny from the 2.11 roster pass. alan, donald, commissioner and devil were generated and REJECTED -- see rejected below. Every fighter without an accepted sheet keeps the pre-2.10 base-only walk byte-identically through the descriptor's chained fallback, so a partial roster costs nothing.
format.gate: walk30/gate.py. W1a contact stride separation >= 60% of the fighter's base mean; W1b passing separation <= 55% of the contact mean; W1c a contact key plants TWO feet and a passing key exactly ONE; W1d the lead leg INVERTS between keys 0 and 2, measured by the near/far shading discriminator (a right-facing figure shows its LEFT side, so the near limbs are lit and the far limbs shadowed; the sign of forward-minus-rear leg luminance must flip); W1e adjacent-key silhouette IoU < 0.75; W2 head-band width spread <= 12% and head-region palette <= 3.0 dE; W4 foot bottoms within 6px.
format.gateCalibration: Two metrics in the original spec were re-derived because they cannot score a walk cycle. (1) CHEST-band width: it is dominated by the swinging arms, not the build -- probed across the roster, a KNOWN-GOOD single-generation sheet spreads 1.2-31.1% on that band, so the literal 12% is unreachable by construction. The head band is pose-invariant and is gated instead; the chest band is reported as advisory. (2) PALETTE: the legs/feet regions are sampled by height fraction, so a contact key (legs spread, background between them) and a passing key (legs overlapping) sample different content of the SAME character -- alone worth 8-12 dE on jez while his head and torso sit at 0.4-1.8. The head region occupies the same pixels in every key and is gated instead. The gate was validated against the BASE bank as a negative control: pointed at base cells 4-7 it fails W1b, W1c, W1d and W1e on every fighter, which is the documented single-phase defect.
format.notGenerated: None. The 2.11 wave generated all eight remaining fighters (17 fal calls). The decisive prompt move on top of the pilot's 1x4 filmstrip + occlusion + tonal grammar was to bind the near/far tonal rule to a NAMED, TRACKABLE COSTUME OBJECT -- 'the black shoe' / 'the pale hoof' / 'the hand holding the spray can' -- and then to restate the whole cycle as a one-line object sequence at the end of the prompt ('black boot behind, black boot lifted, black boot in front, black boot planted'). Every sheet that cleared W1d carried that closing line; the four rounds written with abstract 'bright leg / dark leg' language alone drew the SAME lead leg in both contact keys. Where the two legs wear the same colour the model will not invent the value split, so a fighter in uniformly dark trousers (alan, donald, commissioner) is the hard case: pushing the split hard enough to measure pushes the garment out of its base bank's value range, which is how commissioner lost W3 after winning W1d.

devil.reason: W3 IDENTITY FAIL, second wave running -- but for a DIFFERENT reason than the pilot's, and the pilot's two objections are now fixed. The 2.11 round 3 sheet passes EVERY numeric gate: contact separation 145.5/147.0 against a base mean of 189.8, passing separation 52.0/0, ground-contact runs 2/1/2/1, adjacent-key IoU max 0.545, head-width spread 6.0%, head-region palette 0.8 dE, foot bottoms flat at 315, and a clean inversion at +56.0 / -39.5. The creature is now thick-muscled and heavy-shouldered with full-span wings, so 'spindly with markedly smaller wings' no longer applies. What fails now is HEAD STRUCTURE, read at 2.4x against base cells 0 and 4: the candidate's horns are a tall tight spiral rising ABOVE the skull where the base's sweep back and down in a long arc along the neck; its snout is short and dog-like against the base's long tapering horse-like muzzle; its head is markedly smaller relative to the body and sits on a short thick neck where the base carries a long neck with the head thrust forward and down; and its posture is an upright human bodybuilder's where the base is hunched and forward-leaning. The hide also grades warm golden-brown, measured (97,70,42) over the torso band against the base's muted grey-brown (71,54,40). Different individual, same species -- the same verdict as 2.10, arrived at from the opposite direction.
devil.physiologyNote: Authored as an UPRIGHT BIPEDAL walk, deliberately NOT the all-fours prowl the brief called for. The devil's base atlas is bipedal in every walk and idle cell (verified at 1:1), and MOTION-ATLAS already records that the 2.9 motion2 prowl pair moved his head ~140px in one tick against the upright base cycle. A self-contained prowl bank would not strobe mid-cycle but WOULD fail W5 by construction, because entering and leaving the walk would swap his whole body plan against the idle. The brief's premise that he is a quadruped does not match the shipped art. Re-confirmed in 2.11: all four rounds were authored UPRIGHT BIPEDAL for the same reason, and the bipedal reading is not what failed -- the head and horn structure is.
devil.roundsNote: 2.11 spent all four of its allotted attempts. Round 1 failed W1a (contact separation 85.0 against the 113.8 needed -- his base bank's 189.8 mean stride is the roster's widest and is genuinely hard to match) and W2 head-width 16.4%. Round 2 came within 1.8px of W1a at 112.0 but drew keys 0 and 2 as effectively the same image (IoU 0.960). Round 3 cleared everything numeric. Round 4 chased the identity fix -- cool grey-brown hide, hunched posture, larger head, clawed feet instead of hooves -- and got the stride (149.0/170.0) and the inversion (+68.0 / -60.6) but blew W2 apart at 99.4% head-width spread, with key heights swinging 231-274px. Round 3 remains the best sheet and it is still not the same devil.

Round 1: W1a/b/c/e, W2 and W4 all pass, W1d escalates to the eye at +21.0 / +4.9 -- and the eye call goes AGAINST it, because the shoe-level re-check reads +18.7 / +1.9, no inversion; the golf club and the near arm swap between the contact keys but the legs do not follow, the same defect the commissioner showed. Round 2: W1d clean (+38.2 / -15.2, shoe-level +37.7 / -37.8) but W2 head-region palette 3.6 dE over the 3.0 gate. commissioner.reason: W3 IDENTITY FAIL on the one round that cleared the phase gate. Round 2 passes every numeric gate and passes them well -- contact separation 103.5/101.5 against a base mean of 124.8, runs 2/1/2/1, adjacent IoU max 0.592, head-width 2.3%, head palette 0.7 dE, foot bottoms within 1px, and the widest inversion of the wave at +125.8 / -98.2 -- but it bought that inversion by painting the near leg near-WHITE. Measured over the lower-body band (0.62-0.90 of figure height) the candidate runs mean luminance 60.1/59.2 with a p95 of 184.4, against the base bank's 29.7/34.1 with a p95 of 76.8-94.4: twice as bright, with the top of its range more than double the brightest trouser pixel the base bank owns. In game he would leave a charcoal-trousered idle and enter the walk in white trousers and a white shoe. Every other costume element is excellent -- silver swept-back hair, black leather trench to the knee with the crimson lining, dark red open-collared shirt with the gold chain, black gloves, silver-ball cane -- which is what makes the trouser value the whole of the fault.
commissioner.otherRounds: Round 1 and round 3 both keep the trousers correctly dark (round 3's band reads mean 31.1 / p95 63.7, a good match for the base) and both FAIL W1d: +17.3 / +21.5 and +22.3 / +6.8. In both, the CANE and the near arm swap correctly between the contact keys while the legs stay on the same lead -- proof that the model will follow a prop instruction without following the leg instruction, and the reason the wave's other sheets bind the tonal rule to the SHOE rather than to the hand.
commissioner.registrationNote: Registration was never the problem. His base bank is the roster's one height outlier (walk cells 299/287/280/248 where every other fighter is a flat 304-306, and MOTION_SHEET_ADJUST carries a 1.033 correction for his oversized base sheet), but the walk slicer normalises the tallest key to the fighter's OWN measured base walk height -- 299px for him -- so his sheets landed at 297-299px with foot bottoms within 1px and would have needed no WALK_SHEET_ADJUST entry. The coat also behaved: prompting the panels to flare back kept both legs and both shoes as separate shapes, so W1a and W1c read cleanly instead of the merged-feet blob his base cells produce.
